items.title: Mike Longo interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 13, 2019
items.q: Lorraine got mad at Dizzy ‘cause this woman asked Dizzy... Lorraine got mad.

ctx.x: There’s a movie called A Night in Havanna. And Lorraine got mad at Dizzy ‘cause this woman asked Dizzy, she said, “Where does your music come from?” He said, “You really want to know?” She said, “Yeah.” He said, “My asshole.” And everybody — © Fillius Jazz Archive -18-

Lorraine got mad. But he was serious. Because the energy at the base of your spine man, if you look up the thing called kundalini energy, that’s a part of our music. Now if you notice, there’s a history of Beethoven grunting all the time. Oscar Peterson grunted. Erroll Gardner grunted. Because they’re coming from that base of the spine kind of — and that’s got to be in the music. If that’s not there you’re playing without a bottom to your music. Now that energy there is pretty much a metaphysical thing that…
